about.title: El Cerrito Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Whether you work a warehouse floor near I-80, drive delivery routes through Potrero Avenue traffic, or handle equipment at a Rt 123 job site, a workplace injury in El Cerrito usually starts with a workers' compensation claim through your employer. That system covers most medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but it doesn't account for pain and suffering, and it isn't your only avenue if someone outside your employer contributed to the accident. A subcontractor's negligence, defective machinery, or a careless driver on San Pablo Avenue during a work errand can open the door to a separate third-party injury claim. Because Contra Costa County job sites vary from retail counters to construction crews to logistics hubs near the freeway, the right path depends heavily on the facts of your case. LawProactive connects injured workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, so you can understand both your workers' comp rights and any additional claims worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cerrito Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Workers' Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California generally makes workers' comp your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be liable separately. An attorney can help you sort out which path applies to your situation.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California, and you have 30 days to notify your employer. An attorney in our network can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after reporting an injury.

items.title: Awareness of Claim Deadlines
items.desc: If a third party contributed to your injury, that separate claim carries a two-year deadline in California. Missing that window can close off compensation options beyond workers' comp, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near I-80 in El Cerrito. Is workers' comp my only option?
items.answer: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. But if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the incident, you may have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. An independent attorney can review the details and let you know what applies.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days. Waiting too long can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's best to notify your employer as soon as you're able after the incident.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No. Retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options.

items.question: What if my work injury happened while driving through El Cerrito for my job?
items.answer: If another driver caused a crash while you were on the job, for example along San Pablo Avenue or Potrero Avenue, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party claim against that driver. These claims run on different timelines, so it helps to have someone review the specifics early.
